title: Fixed Whole Transverse Slats and Laced Cords Makisu
description: One newly authored complete empty makisu-inspired bamboo rolling-mat appearance in one fixed partly curled pose. Twenty-four whole long transverse slats have finite flattened lower faces, curved bevelled upper sections and complete bevelled cut ends. Four entire closed lacing circuits each form two uninterrupted narrow opposite-phase over-under routes along all slats, returning at both ends. The broad front portion lies low while the rear slat sequence rises into an open inward curl; real narrow air intervals remain between the slats and no filled sheet replaces the bamboo field. All slat cross-sections, stations, curled centre route and complete lacing paths are original numerical geometry. Unlike the long agility ladder with widely spaced slotted rungs and two broad straps passing inside the rung holes, these unperforated close-set full-width rods are externally encircled by returning alternating narrow cords. Unlike the elevated one-sided warp loom there is no supporting side frame, cantilever pegs, winding polygon, heddle or separate working thread span. Twenty-eight complete closed editable meshes, four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres native Z up and horizontal whole-bounds-centred ground datum. One whole independent model zero scenes; the slats and laces are not separately counted. Ground contact is through finite lower cord facets; all slats have explicit small static lacing contacts. Category-level artistic exterior only, not a measured museum or branded product, and not a claim of exact traditional knot or weaving topology. The compact fixed return circuits are a simplified visual binding, not a manufactured textile fastening specification. No sushi, other food, hand, film, water or cookware included.
